feedback.worked_solution:
If $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ is a vector field and $C$ is a piecewise-smooth, simple curve, then the flux of $F$ across $C$ measured with respect to a unit normal vector $n$ on $C$ is given by

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={\int }_{C}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x.
$$

To apply this formula, 

- the curve should be parameterized as $r(t)$ for $t\in [a,b],$ and

- the unit normal vector $n$ *must* be a ${90}^{∘}$ clockwise rotation of the unit tangent vector $T(t).$

Parameterizing the line segment $L,$ we have

$$
x=\sqrt{2}t,\,y=-\sqrt{2}t,\,t\in [0,1].
$$

 

This parameterization traverses the line from the point $(0,0)$ to the point $(\sqrt{2},-\sqrt{2}).$ Therefore, $n$ is indeed a ${90}^{∘}$ clockwise rotation of $T,$ so we can apply the above formula for the flux. 

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(x,y) & =3x{y}^{2} \\  & =3(\sqrt{2}t)(-\sqrt{2}t)^{2} \\  & =6\sqrt{2}{t}^{3}, \\ Q(x,y) & =-{y}^{3} \\  & =-(-\sqrt{2}t)^{3} \\  & =2\sqrt{2}{t}^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing the derivatives of $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ along the curve, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}t)=\sqrt{2}, \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\sqrt{2}t)=-\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{L}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{L}P\,\text{d}y-Q\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(P\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}-Q\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(6\sqrt{2}{t}^{3})\cdot (-\sqrt{2})-(2\sqrt{2}{t}^{3})\cdot (\sqrt{2})\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(-12{t}^{3}-4{t}^{3})\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}-16{t}^{3}\,\text{d}t \\  & =-4[{t}^{4}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =-4(1-0) \\  & =-4\end{aligned}
$$
